exchanges.question: I need to change the die on the HP-400. What do I have to do?
exchanges.answer: To change the die on the HP-400, first lower the ram onto the die, then perform a full lockout by disconnecting DS-400, bleed the accumulator to 0 psi at valve HV-2, and insert both ram safety blocks from the red storage rack. Never enter the die area without these safety steps. Next, unclamp and remove the die using the die cart; do not slide dies by hand. Install the new die, center it with the locating pins, and torque the die clamp bolts to 250 N·m (184 ft·lb) in a cross pattern. After installation, remove the blocks and locks, set the shut height per the die setup sheet, and run a first-article part for quality control. The first-article inspection must be verified and signed before production continues. [1][2][3][4][5]

exchanges.question: What PPE do I need to clean the solvent tank?
exchanges.answer: For cleaning the solvent tank of PW-1, you need nitrile gloves (minimum 15 mil), chemical splash goggles, and a chemical-resistant apron. Additionally, local exhaust ventilation must be running during use. If the ventilation is not running, you must wear a half-face respirator with organic vapor cartridges, and respirator users must be fit-tested within the last 12 months. Inspect PPE before use and replace as necessary. [1][2][3]

exchanges.question: What torque do the HP-400 die clamp bolts need?
exchanges.answer: The HP-400 die clamp bolts need to be torqued to 250 N·m (184 ft·lb). Torque the bolts in a cross pattern during die installation. [1][2]

exchanges.question: Where is the evacuation assembly point?
exchanges.answer: The evacuation assembly point is Area B in the north parking lot. After evacuating, the floor supervisor takes the shift roster, completes a headcount within 10 minutes, and reports any missing people to the incident commander. No one should re-enter until EHS gives the all-clear. [1]

exchanges.question: What do I do with a part that fails inspection?
exchanges.answer: If a part fails inspection, stop the process and notify the floor supervisor. Hold all parts made since the last in-control subgroup and check them 100% for the affected characteristic. Find and correct the cause of the failure, note it on the chart, and run a First-Article Inspection (FAI) before restarting production. Only the Material Review Board (MRB) may disposition nonconforming parts; operators and supervisors cannot rework, use, or scrap parts on their own. The MRB can decide to use as is (with approvals), rework (with instructions and 100% re-inspection), scrap (mark with red paint and record), or return to supplier (with SCAR issued). [1][2][3]
